doc.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

chapter: From The Lancers to Harry James
title: Seattle, Gina Funes, and eloping with Joe Venuti
summary: He settled in Seattle with a yacht club contract, met singer Gina Funes, and eloped with Joe Venuti's encouragement.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Seattle you call me, I’ll hire you.” Because he had a band that worked five nights a week. So I had her phone number and called her up, and she says, “I’m serious,” she said, “it’s funny you should call, Fred, I’m looking for a band to start next week. How would you like a year contract?” I said, “Really? Okay you got it.” I said, “I’ll be there.” So I called the best musicians in Seattle, which are really good player, a rhythm section. I get in my car and I’m thinking Jesus, I need a place to stay, I didn’t think about this. So now I have another friend of mind that lived on Bainbridge Island and he had this beach house that was right on the beach in Manitou Beach. And you walk out and in those days Bainbridge Island — it was a summer place. Not many people wintered there. And there’s Seattle, you’re right on Puget Sound. And there’s the whole city landscape. So I called this guy up and said, “You know I’m thinking of coming to Seattle, I’ve got a gig at the Edmonds Yacht Club for a year and we’re going to do it.” And he says, “It’s funny you should call” he says, “we’re going to the desert for six months. Why don’t you come and stay at the house?” And I said, “Well I can’t afford” and he says, “No I just want somebody to stay here.” “Okay.” So now I have a pad and a gig. So here I go. I go to Seattle and start working, and naturally The Lancers were pretty well known. So when I showed up into town to do any extra shows, everybody kind of moved down a chair. You know I said, don’t get me wrong I mean — but they said, “Fred Radke’s in town,” everybody — when you went out on a gig the guy that used to play lead now moved down. Nothing was said. And so we played the Olympic Hotel, which they had a big showroom, and they had a singer there that had just come from the Johnny Carson show and she was the longest running act at the Hungry Eye in San Francisco and she was very well known. She was opera-trained but she was a nightclub singer and a very elegant lady, just an incredible singer. And so her piano player decides to go to Nashville to join somebody and so she says well who am I going to get for my conductor. And he says, “Well you remember Fred Radke that played opposite —” She said, “I don’t want a trumpet player, are you kidding? So that’s my wife Gina Funes. We’ve been married going on 58 years, okay. And so we were starting to work shows together after I left the yacht club. And so we were going to work a convention and Joe Venuti lived in Seattle, the world’s greatest violinist.

And so we did these shows together. And so we’re driving to Spokane and he’s in the back seat and he says, “You know you guys are perfect for each other. You should get married.” And we said, “Well we’ve been talking about it.” “Oh you’ve got to get married. Why don’t we go elope.” So we didn’t stop at Spokane, we went to Cour d’Alene and we eloped.
